intro: Across India and East Asia, people light lamps, ring bells, share free meals and bow to their grandparents. These actions come from some of the oldest traditions in the world. Millions of people follow them today, including many families in Chicago.

In this unit you will meet Hinduism and Buddhism, then Sikhism, Jainism, and the teachings of Confucius and the Dao. You will learn their stories, words, holidays and practices. You will see what adherents believe and why their practices matter to them.
By the end, you will be able to explain key words, match practices to traditions and compare how each tradition teaches people to live well. You will describe each one fairly, in its own words.
bigQuestion: How do traditions from India and East Asia teach people to live a good life?

timeline.t: The oldest Hindu Vedas begin to be composed in northern India
Mahavira teaches ahimsa, the Jain way of non-harm
Siddhartha Gautama becomes the Buddha, Buddhists teach
Confucius teaches in China; his students later write the Analects
The Daodejing is known in China, linked by tradition to Laozi
The Bhagavad Gita takes shape; dates are debated by scholars
Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, is born in the Punjab
Guru Gobind Singh begins the Khalsa and the five Ks
Hindu, Buddhist and Jain speakers address the Parliament of Religions in Chicago
Chicago has Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh and Jain houses of worship

words.d: in Hindu teaching, the one great spirit behind everything
Hindu worship with offerings, light and prayer
action; the idea that actions bring results
duty or right way to live; for Buddhists, also the Buddha's teaching
the belief that a soul is born again in a new body
in Buddhism, waking up to the truth about life and suffering
in Buddhism, the end of suffering and craving
the free meal at every gurdwara, open to all
the Sikh holy book, honored as the living Guru
non-violence; doing no harm to any living being
respect and care for parents and elders, taught by Confucius
"the way"; in Daoism, the natural flow behind all things

test.q: Which tradition has the Vedas as its oldest texts?
test.why: The Vedas are the oldest Hindu scriptures.

test.q: What do many Hindus call a person's soul?
test.why: Atman is the Hindu word for the soul.

test.q: What did Siddhartha see that made him leave the palace?
test.why: The four sights showed him suffering and a calm monk.

test.q: What is the Buddhist path to end suffering called?
test.why: The fourth Noble Truth is the Eightfold Path.

test.q: What does the Dhammapada's first verse say shapes who we are?
test.why: It says all that we are is the result of what we have thought.

test.q: Which branch of Buddhism is called the way of the elders?
test.why: Theravada means the way of the elders.
Guru Nanak was the first Sikh Guru.
Gurdwara means door of the Guru.

test.q: What is the main reason Jains are careful not to harm insects?
choices: They believe all living things have souls
It is part of Lunar New Year
test.why: Jain ahimsa rests on the belief that every being has a soul.

test.q: Which saying comes from Confucius's Analects?
choices: Truth is one, the wise call it by many names
What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others
There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim
All that we are is the result of what we have thought
test.why: Analects 15.23 gives this rule of reciprocity.

test.q: What do yin and yang stand for?
test.why: Yin and yang are opposites that need each other.

test.q: Which tradition is linked to the Daodejing?
test.why: The Daodejing is the best-known Daoist book.

test.q: Which word do Hindus, Buddhists and Jains all use, in their own ways?
test.why: All three Indian traditions teach about karma.

test.q: Which is the fairest way to write about these traditions?
choices: Hindus believe..., Jains teach..., in each tradition's own words
Say one is better than the others
Use only one tradition's words for all
test.why: Attribute each belief and describe without ranking.

write.prompt: How should people treat others? Choose two traditions from this unit. Use one text or practice from each, such as the langar, the Analects, a Jain teaching or the Eightfold Path. Explain what each tradition teaches and why.
tips: Name the text or practice you use.
Say who believes it: "Sikhs teach..." or "Confucius said..."
Tell how the two are alike and how they are different.
Use at least three words from this unit.
Compare; do not judge which is better.
